newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed on Friday in moderate post-holiday trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.

"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market after the May Day holiday on Thursday. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.

In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.45/1.40 percent compared with Wednesday's yield of 1.49/1.44 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.58/1.53 percent against Wednesday's yield of 1.60/1.55 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$99.61/99.71 from Wednesday's close of S$99.60/99.65, September 2001 at S$96.90/96.95 versus S$96.89/96.94 and June 2003 at S$94.92/94.97 against $S94.90/94.95.
The interbank rate rose slightly to 3-9/16 3-7/16 percent from Wednesday's 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent.
